# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit

- **State**: open

- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163

- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

    "description": "Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun."

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit

- **State**: open

- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

1. **`l10n:ignore-file` comment at the top of `codemie_sso_flow_steps.dart`** — "SSO flow screens — en-only by design (EPAM-internal tooling)". So hardcoded English strings in `showCodeMieNamePrompt` ARE consistent with the file's convention. Good — not an issue.

2. **`saveCodemieConnection` update branch**: 
```dart
if (existing != null) {
    final updated = CustomProvider(
      id: existing.id,
      name: existing.name,   // ← NOT the new `name` param!
      baseUrl: baseUrl,
      modelId: modelId,
    );
```
The update branch uses `existing.name`, IGNORING the `name` parameter. In `_completeSignIn`, `existingByName` is derived via byName(name) with baseUrl equality — so `existingByName.name` should equal `name` (case-insensitively at least; byName folds case, so if the user typed different case — "Work" vs stored "work" — byName matches the stored "work" entry, and `saveCodemieConnection` keeps `existing.name` = "work". So the user-typed casing is silently discarded on the update path. That's... actually consistent: landing by name → the stored entry keeps its name. Fine, not a bug per se — the update keeps the entry's identity. Actually wait, but consider `_completeSignIn`: `name` typed = "WORK", target=byName → stored entry "work" on same baseUrl → existingByName = that entry → update keeps "work". The user's casing ignored, but no data corruption. OK.

But there's a subtle inconsistency: in `saveCodemieConnection`, when `existing == null` the add path uses `name`. When `existing != null`, name param is unused (except implicitly through the caller's existingByName). A nit: `name` is ignored in the update branch — could confuse future callers. Minor SUGGESTION.

3. **`_completeExtensionSignin`**: `existing` is looked up by `p.baseUrl == baseUrl` (firstOrNull). It passes `name: existing?.name ?? codeMieHostFromUrl(orgUrl)` and `existing: existing`. But hold on — if there are now MULTIPLE entries on the same baseUrl (the multi-account feature!), `registry.providers.where((p) => p.baseUrl == baseUrl).firstOrNull` picks the FIRST one — the extension re-login would update the first entry by URL, NOT by name. But the extension branch has no name step (documented: "one browser jar carries one session"), so updating... which one? The FIRST by insertion order. If a user has two CodeMie accounts on the same org via SSO and then connects via the extension branch, the extension login overwrites whichever entry is first — arbitrary! Before this PR there could only be ONE entry per endpoint (well, the editor path could have added duplicates before this PR — the "always added" bug). Hmm, but with multi-account coexistence now possible, the extension branch's by-URL-first lookup silently picks an arbitrary account. Is that a real problem? The extension cookie jar has ONE session; the user logs in as some account; the app can't know which entry corresponds. Updating the first match is a heuristic. The PR explicitly says "Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session" — but keeps the FIRST entry's name and updates the FIRST entry, which may be the WRONG account entry (overwriting account B's model with account A's entry... well the key is jar-based anyway; key: '' for both). Actually since the extension stores key='' (jar auth), updating entry A vs B mostly changes modelId. Low severity, but worth noting as SUGGESTION: extension branch's firstOrNull-by-URL becomes ambiguous with multi-account entries; consider updating by name too, or the most-recently-used.

Actually wait — more subtle: `_completeExtensionSignin` passes `existing: existing` where existing was fetched by URL. But in `_completeSignIn` (SSO branch), they now deliberately changed to by-NAME lookup (`existingByName`) for the update target. The extension branch still uses by-URL. Inconsistent — but documented. I'll note as a suggestion.

4. **`saveCodemieConnection` update branch drops `requiresKey`, `provenance`, `kind`** — `CustomProvider(id, name, baseUrl, modelId)` — check CustomProvider's constructor defaults. In `landProviderResult` the update preserves `requiresKey/provenance/kind` from existing. But `saveCodemieConnection`'s update does NOT preserve them (it never did — pre-existing behavior). Hmm, was that pre-existing? The diff only changed `name:` addition; the update branch was `CustomProvider(id: existing.id, name: existing.name, baseUrl: baseUrl, modelId: modelId)` before too (the diff shows only `-    final name = codeMieHostFromUrl(orgUrl);` removed and the add branch changed). So pre-existing behavior; not introduced by this PR. Skip or minor mention.

5. **Controller leak / rebuild in `showCodeMieNamePrompt`**: The `TextEditingController` is created inside `showDialog`'s builder — recreated every time the dialog route's builder re-runs. When does that happen? `showDialog` builder is invoked on route rebuild — MediaQuery changes (keyboard!), theme changes. With `autofocus: true`, when the dialog opens on mobile, the keyboard animates in → MediaQuery viewInsets change → the Dialog route rebuilds? The dialog builder's context — the builder function of the route is called on route setState and on inherited dependencies changes. The `TextField` inside depends on `MediaQuery` (via Material/ScrollConfiguration etc.). When MediaQuery changes, elements rebuild but the ROUTE's builder function is NOT re-invoked (the builder result is cached in the route's widget tree; builder is only called when the route's `_DialogWidget` rebuilds... hmm).

Actually let me think about Flutter internals: `showDialog` creates a `DialogRoute` with a `pageBuilder`/builder. The route builds `_DialogWidget` (a stateful widget) which calls `route.buildPage(context, ...)` — buildPage is called on every rebuild of `_DialogWidget`'s state (it's called in `build` → `ModalRoute.buildPage` is invoked when the route's `setState` or dependencies change... `_DialogWidgetState.build` calls `widget.route.buildPage(...)`. `_DialogWidget` is a `Widget` that gets rebuilt when the route calls `setState` (animations) or when inherited widgets change. Hmm — actually `_DialogWidgetState` has `didChangeDependencies` → `setState`? ModalRoute's `_ModalScope` rebuilds on route changes (animation, etc.). The captured `builder` closure would then re-run, creating a NEW TextEditingController — losing user input.

But in practice: does the keyboard appearing trigger a rebuild of the dialog widget? The `MediaQuery` viewInsets change on keyboard show. The dialog's Material Scaffold? No Scaffold — the dialog is a `Dialog` inside `SafeArea`? AlertDialog's content doesn't depend on MediaQuery directly for viewInsets... Actually `MediaQuery` is inherited; the dialog widget tree includes `MediaQuery.removeViewInsets`? Hmm. `AlertDialog` itself — the `Dialog` widget uses `MediaQueryData.viewInsets` to avoid the keyboard: yes! `Dialog` reads `MediaQuery.of(context).viewInsets` to inset itself above the keyboard. So when the keyboard appears (autofocus opens it), viewInsets change → `Dialog`'s dependency on MediaQuery changes → `_DialogWidget`... wait the dependency is registered by the `Dialog` widget inside the builder's returned tree, not by `_DialogWidget` itself. Rebuilds propagate to the exact widget that registered the dependency (the Dialog element), not up to `_DialogWidget`. The builder would NOT re-run for that.

However, `StatefulBuilder`'s setState → rebuilds only its subtree. So the controller is created once per `_DialogWidget` build. When does `_DialogWidget` rebuild? On route animation ticks (during open/close only), on `route.setState` from textScale changes? `ModalRoute.setState` is called on `changeTextScaleFactor`? There's `route.annotation`, `offstage`... Critical scenario (same-endpoint rename collision in EDIT mode):
- Entry "A" (id 1) and entry "B" (id 2), both baseUrl E.
- Edit "A": editor with initial = A. Rename to "B", Save.
- `_save` clash check: `clash = byName("B")` → entry B (id 2). `clash.id != widget.initial?.id` → 2 != 1 → true. `clash.baseUrl != baseUrl` → E != E → false. → condition false → NOT rejected. Pop result(name "B", baseUrl E).
- The edit caller (Providers section) presumably does `registry.update(CustomProvider(id: 1, name: "B", ...))` → now TWO entries named "B" on endpoint E → the ambiguity this PR is meant to eliminate, plus `byName("B")` returns the first → future reconnects would update the wrong entry.

So the "same endpoint = re-connect shape" rule conflates CONNECT (add flow, where updating by name is right) and EDIT (where renaming to a colliding name on the same endpoint should be rejected). Unless the edit caller rejects it... Let me check the ProvidersSection edit handler.

The PR claims "Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a different endpoint (inline error)" — but only when `registry` is passed to the editor. In `_addProvider` and `_addProviderFromCta` (settings.dart:1928), the editor has no registry → no rejection, and the landing is a plain `add` → both the name-clash and the duplicate-endpoint behaviors persist on those paths. Same for `model_presets.dart:_setupKey` — no registry (only saves key to keysStore — different concern, doesn't add providers. Fine.)

   So the PR fixes fa_ui's picker/editor/section and the app's SSO flow, but the app-level settings screen paths (`_addProvider`, `_addProviderFromCta`, `_editProvider`) still use the old unguarded pattern:
   - `_addProvider` (no registry → no clash check, unconditional add → duplicates).
   - `_addProviderFromCta` (same).
   - `_editProvider` HAS `registry: _registry` → clash check runs; rename to same-endpoint colliding name allowed → duplicate names (invariant break); but rename to other-endpoint colliding name rejected. Also, `_editProvider` still lands via `registry.update` directly — fine for edit.

   Are these in scope? The PR is about "app add-provider flow". The settings screen `_addProvider` IS an app add-provider flow (arguably the primary one before the picker page existed). This is a genuine gap worth flagging as IMPORTANT — the fix is inconsistent across the app's add-provider entries: the same bug class persists at `settings.dart:_addProvider` and `_addProviderFromCta`. Let me check quickly.

3. **`_editPreset`**: preset editor in ProvidersSection — name editable, `initial: null`, registry passed. Rename a hosted preset entry to a name colliding on the same endpoint → allowed → duplicate names. Same invariant break. And baseUrl in preset mode is prefilled from preset; user could CHANGE the baseUrl (editable in preset mode per docstring!). # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

Very valuable context. Key facts about CLI parity:

1. CLI `find(name)` is case-insensitive — the new app `byName` case-insensitivity matches the CLI. ✓ parity claim holds.

2. CLI's `add` **throws on reserved (catalog) names** — "the interactive name prompts reject these names already, this is the last line of defense". The app's new `landProviderResult` and fa_ui `ProviderRegistry.add` have NO reserved-name guard, and the app prompts don't reject catalog names (`openai`, `codemie`, `kimi`...). BUT does the app registry persist to the same `providers.json` / config as the CLI? The fa_ui ProviderRegistry persists to `providers.json` under ExecutionEnv.cwd — a DIFFERENT store than the CLI's config.yaml customProviders. So catalog-name shadowing (`/provider <name>` routing) is CLI-only and doesn't cross stores. So missing catalog-name rejection in the app is NOT a parity bug per se (the CLI rationale is `/provider` routing, which doesn't exist in the app). OK — not an issue beyond CLI-vs-app store separation.

3. However `isUsableCustomProviderName` — the CLI validates names against `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+:@-]*$` because names with `?`/whitespace/quotes corrupt YAML (issue #555). But the app registry persists to providers.json (JSON), not YAML. Wait — actually is the app's ProviderRegistry writing config.yaml or providers.json? `static const fileName = 'providers.json'`. So YAML corruption is not a concern for the app store. But wait — do app-created providers end up in the CLI's config? The PR description mentions "same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (FA_KEY_<HOST> hydration)" — implying keychain slots ARE shared with the CLI, but the provider entries themselves live in providers.json (app) vs config.yaml customProviders (CLI). Two different stores. OK.

So the missing name-validation in the app prompt is a low-severity observation: a name with leading/trailing whitespace is trimmed; but names like `?`, `my provider` (space), `#work`, emoji are allowed by the app while the CLI would reject them. Since stores are separate, impact is cosmetic. Also the app byName trims input but stored names are compared untrimmed. Minor.

4. CLI `_askConnectProviderName` ALSO checks catalog names — skip.

Now, the CRITICAL parity check — the CLI convention "add-replaces-on-name-clash": CLI `CustomProviderRegistry.add` = "Adds (or replaces, on name clash)". The app's fa_ui `ProviderRegistry.add` — does it replace on name clash? Let me check. If it doesn't, `landProviderResult` handles it — fine. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

Key facts:

1. `ProviderRegistry.add` does NOT replace on name clash — it always appends. So the CLI "add-replaces-on-name-clash" convention is implemented only inside `landProviderResult`, NOT in `registry.add` itself. All OTHER app callers of `registry.add` remain unconditional adds: they can still mint same-name duplicates (no guard), and once duplicates exist, `byName` silently targets the first. This is the documented known follow-up: two same-host entries share one keychain slot. Also notice: `rememberKey` from `landProviderResult`/`saveCodemieConnection` → keychain write keyed by baseUrl host. The second CodeMie account's cookie would OVERWRITE the first account's keychain slot. And `add()` re-picks up `remembered` key from the shared slot. This is acknowledged in the PR description as a known follow-up — OK, documented. But worth surfacing in review as a data-loss-ish caveat: account A's persisted key is silently replaced by account B's after restart. Documented = not blocking, but I might list under "known limitations acknowledged by the author" in the general comment.

3. `update()` matches by id and no-ops when absent — `landProviderResult` reads `existing` then updates; race-free enough for UI.

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.
