# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

Critical scenario (same-endpoint rename collision in EDIT mode):
- Entry "A" (id 1) and entry "B" (id 2), both baseUrl E.
- Edit "A": editor with initial = A. Rename to "B", Save.
- `_save` clash check: `clash = byName("B")` → entry B (id 2). `clash.id != widget.initial?.id` → 2 != 1 → true. `clash.baseUrl != baseUrl` → E != E → false. → condition false → NOT rejected. Pop result(name "B", baseUrl E).
- The edit caller (Providers section) presumably does `registry.update(CustomProvider(id: 1, name: "B", ...))` → now TWO entries named "B" on endpoint E → the ambiguity this PR is meant to eliminate, plus `byName("B")` returns the first → future reconnects would update the wrong entry.

So the "same endpoint = re-connect shape" rule conflates CONNECT (add flow, where updating by name is right) and EDIT (where renaming to a colliding name on the same endpoint should be rejected). Unless the edit caller rejects it... Let me check the ProvidersSection edit handler.

Very valuable context. Key facts about CLI parity:

1. CLI `find(name)` is case-insensitive — the new app `byName` case-insensitivity matches the CLI. ✓ parity claim holds.

2. CLI's `add` **throws on reserved (catalog) names** — "the interactive name prompts reject these names already, this is the last line of defense". The app's new `landProviderResult` and fa_ui `ProviderRegistry.add` have NO reserved-name guard, and the app prompts don't reject catalog names (`openai`, `codemie`, `kimi`...). BUT does the app registry persist to the same `providers.json` / config as the CLI? The fa_ui ProviderRegistry persists to `providers.json` under ExecutionEnv.cwd — a DIFFERENT store than the CLI's config.yaml customProviders. So catalog-name shadowing (`/provider <name>` routing) is CLI-only and doesn't cross stores. So missing catalog-name rejection in the app is NOT a parity bug per se (the CLI rationale is `/provider` routing, which doesn't exist in the app). OK — not an issue beyond CLI-vs-app store separation.

3. However `isUsableCustomProviderName` — the CLI validates names against `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+:@-]*$` because names with `?`/whitespace/quotes corrupt YAML (issue #555). But the app registry persists to providers.json (JSON), not YAML. Wait — actually is the app's ProviderRegistry writing config.yaml or providers.json? `static const fileName = 'providers.json'`. So YAML corruption is not a concern for the app store. But wait — do app-created providers end up in the CLI's config? The PR description mentions "same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (FA_KEY_<HOST> hydration)" — implying keychain slots ARE shared with the CLI, but the provider entries themselves live in providers.json (app) vs config.yaml customProviders (CLI). Two different stores. OK.

So the missing name-validation in the app prompt is a low-severity observation: a name with leading/trailing whitespace is trimmed; but names like `?`, `my provider` (space), `#work`, emoji are allowed by the app while the CLI would reject them. Key facts:

1. `ProviderRegistry.add` does NOT replace on name clash — it always appends. So the CLI "add-replaces-on-name-clash" convention is implemented only inside `landProviderResult`, NOT in `registry.add` itself. All OTHER app callers of `registry.add` remain unconditional adds: they can still mint same-name duplicates (no guard), and once duplicates exist, `byName` silently targets the first. Confirmed inconsistency.

2. `rememberKey` — interesting: with keychain, `rememberKey(id, key)` stores the key under `keyNameFor(baseUrl)` — HOST-scoped. This is the documented known follow-up: two same-host entries share one keychain slot. Also notice: `rememberKey` from `landProviderResult`/`saveCodemieConnection` → keychain write keyed by baseUrl host. The second CodeMie account's cookie would OVERWRITE the first account's keychain slot. And `add()` re-picks up `remembered` key from the shared slot. This is acknowledged in the PR description as a known follow-up — OK, documented. But worth surfacing in review as a data-loss-ish caveat: account A's persisted key is silently replaced by account B's after restart. Documented = not blocking, but I might list under "known limitations acknowledged by the author" in the general comment.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

Hmm, wait. Let me double check the picker in fa_ui `_onPresetTap` — the onboarding `_P2` at line 215 passes registry to... `_P2` might render `AddProviderPresetPickerPage`? Whether it embeds AddProviderPresetPickerPage or its own preset list: line 1440 `_beginPresetFlow(preset)` → so it's its own list with its own flow → the onboarding key-based path is its own code. OK.

Now let me also verify the claim in `_editPreset` (ProvidersSection): its landing uses by-URL-first (`firstOrNull`), renames the found entry to result.name. With multi-account coexistence, TWO entries may serve the same preset endpoint (e.g., two OpenRouter accounts added as "OpenRouter Work" / "OpenRouter Personal" via the picker — allowed now!). Then `_editPreset` (tapping the preset row in the Providers section, not a custom row) updates the FIRST by URL and renames it to whatever name is typed — could silently rename the wrong account AND collide names. Pre-existing logic, but the PR's new multi-account world makes its ambiguity worse. Worth an IMPORTANT/SUGGESTION. Actually the picker prefill fix means re-adding via preset tile targets the FIRST entry's name too (`byBaseUrl` first match). Editing the SECOND account is only possible through its custom row (`_editCustom`) — which works (initial set, by-id update). OK.

- Entries: "Work" (id 1, endpoint E), "Personal" (id 2, endpoint E) — both created via the new multi-account flow.
- User edits "Personal" and renames it to "work" → clash check: byName("work") → entry 1; clash.id(1) != initial.id(2) → true; clash.baseUrl(E) != baseUrl(E) → FALSE → no rejection → update lands: entry 2 renamed "work" → registry now has TWO entries named "Work"/"work" on E → every picker shows two indistinguishable rows (the ambiguity the PR set out to kill), and `byName("work")` now returns the first → a later CodeMie/re-connect landing targets the wrong entry.

This is a genuine correctness gap in the invariant enforcement: the editor cannot distinguish "add/connect" from "edit" contexts, and the same-endpoint allowance is correct only for add/connect. The fix: reject a name clash on the same endpoint when `clash.id != widget.initial?.id` too (i.e., a different entry on the same endpoint owns the name). For the ADD/CONNECT flows, a same-endpoint name clash has `clash.id == null-initial` mismatch... wait: in add mode `widget.initial` is null → `clash.id != null` is always true → same-endpoint clash would ALSO be rejected under the stricter rule — which would BREAK the re-connect shape (name+endpoint match = update). So the stricter rule needs a mode flag (create vs edit) — e.g., only allow same-endpoint name takeover when `initial == null` (create/re-connect) — in EDIT mode (initial != null), reject ANY name owned by another entry (regardless of endpoint). That's the clean fix: `if (clash != null && clash.id != widget.initial?.id && (widget.initial == null ? clash.baseUrl != baseUrl : true))`. Right — in edit mode, renaming to any other entry's name should be rejected. That's the actionable suggestion.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

Hmm, wait. Let me double check the picker in fa_ui `_onPresetTap` — the onboarding `_P2` at line 215 passes registry to... `_P2` might render `AddProviderPresetPickerPage`? No — line 1440 `_beginPresetFlow` handles taps directly (own flow). Whether it embeds AddProviderPresetPickerPage or its own preset list: line 1440 `_beginPresetFlow(preset)` → so it's its own list with its own flow → the onboarding key-based path is its own code. OK.

Now let me also verify the claim in `_editPreset` (ProvidersSection): its landing uses by-URL-first (`firstOrNull`), renames the found entry to result.name. With multi-account coexistence, TWO entries may serve the same preset endpoint (e.g., two OpenRouter accounts added as "OpenRouter Work" / "OpenRouter Personal" via the picker — allowed now!). Then `_editPreset` (tapping the preset row in the Providers section, not a custom row) updates the FIRST by URL and renames it to whatever name is typed — could silently rename the wrong account AND collide names. Pre-existing logic, but the PR's new multi-account world makes its ambiguity worse. Worth an IMPORTANT/SUGGESTION. Actually the picker prefill fix means re-adding via preset tile targets the FIRST entry's name too (`byBaseUrl` first match). Editing the SECOND account is only possible through its custom row (`_editCustom`) — which works (initial set, by-id update). OK.

- Entries: "Work" (id 1, endpoint E), "Personal" (id 2, endpoint E) — both created via the new multi-account flow.
- User edits "Personal" and renames it to "work" → clash check: byName("work") → entry 1; clash.id(1) != initial.id(2) → true; clash.baseUrl(E) != baseUrl(E) → FALSE → no rejection → update lands: entry 2 renamed "work" → registry now has TWO entries named "Work"/"work" on E → every picker shows two indistinguishable rows (the ambiguity the PR set out to kill), and `byName("work")` now returns the first → a later CodeMie/re-connect landing targets the wrong entry.

This is a genuine correctness gap in the invariant enforcement: the editor cannot distinguish "add/connect" from "edit" contexts, and the same-endpoint allowance is correct only for add/connect. The fix: reject a name clash on the same endpoint when `clash.id != widget.initial?.id` too (i.e., a different entry on the same endpoint owns the name). For the ADD/CONNECT flows, a same-endpoint name clash has `clash.id == null-initial` mismatch... wait: in add mode `widget.initial` is null → `clash.id != null` is always true → same-endpoint clash would ALSO be rejected under the stricter rule — which would BREAK the re-connect shape (name+endpoint match = update). That's the clean fix: `if (clash != null && clash.id != widget.initial?.id && (widget.initial == null ? clash.baseUrl != baseUrl : true))`. Right — in edit mode, renaming to any other entry's name should be rejected. That's the actionable suggestion.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

2. Cross-endpoint name clash → editor rejects (registry passed) → OK.

The flutter_app settings.dart still has its own add path used at line 996 (`onAdd: _addProvider`). It's reachable. So the PR title claims "multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow" — but at least three app add-provider paths retain the old always-add behavior: settings `_addProvider`, settings `_addProviderFromCta`, onboarding `_persistKeyBased`. This is a legit IMPORTANT finding (partial fix / inconsistent landing semantics; users hit different behavior depending on entry point).

Hmm, wait. Let me double check the picker in fa_ui `_onPresetTap` — the onboarding `_P2` at line 215 passes registry to... `_P2` might render `AddProviderPresetPickerPage`? Now let me also verify the claim in `_editPreset` (ProvidersSection): its landing uses by-URL-first (`firstOrNull`), renames the found entry to result.name. With multi-account coexistence, TWO entries may serve the same preset endpoint (e.g., two OpenRouter accounts added as "OpenRouter Work" / "OpenRouter Personal" via the picker — allowed now!). Then `_editPreset` (tapping the preset row in the Providers section, not a custom row) updates the FIRST by URL and renames it to whatever name is typed — could silently rename the wrong account AND collide names. Pre-existing logic, but the PR's new multi-account world makes its ambiguity worse. Worth an IMPORTANT/SUGGESTION. Actually the picker prefill fix means re-adding via preset tile targets the FIRST entry's name too (`byBaseUrl` first match). Editing the SECOND account is only possible through its custom row (`_editCustom`) — which works (initial set, by-id update). OK.

Now the **rename-collision in `_editCustom`/`_editProvider` (same-endpoint)**: concrete scenario:
- Entries: "Work" (id 1, endpoint E), "Personal" (id 2, endpoint E) — both created via the new multi-account flow.
- User edits "Personal" and renames it to "work" → clash check: byName("work") → entry 1; clash.id(1) != initial.id(2) → true; clash.baseUrl(E) != baseUrl(E) → FALSE → no rejection → update lands: entry 2 renamed "work" → registry now has TWO entries named "Work"/"work" on E → every picker shows two indistinguishable rows (the ambiguity the PR set out to kill), and `byName("work")` now returns the first → a later CodeMie/re-connect landing targets the wrong entry.

This is a genuine correctness gap in the invariant enforcement: the editor cannot distinguish "add/connect" from "edit" contexts, and the same-endpoint allowance is correct only for add/connect. The fix: reject a name clash on the same endpoint when `clash.id != widget.initial?.id` too (i.e., a different entry on the same endpoint owns the name). For the ADD/CONNECT flows, a same-endpoint name clash has `clash.id == null-initial` mismatch... wait: in add mode `widget.initial` is null → `clash.id != null` is always true → same-endpoint clash would ALSO be rejected under the stricter rule — which would BREAK the re-connect shape (name+endpoint match = update). Hmm. So the stricter rule needs a mode flag (create vs edit) — e.g., only allow same-endpoint name takeover when `initial == null` (create/re-connect) — in EDIT mode (initial != null), reject ANY name owned by another entry (regardless of endpoint). That's the clean fix: `if (clash != null && clash.id != widget.initial?.id && (widget.initial == null ? clash.baseUrl != baseUrl : true))`. Right — in edit mode, renaming to any other entry's name should be rejected. That's the actionable suggestion.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

Critical scenario (same-endpoint rename collision in EDIT mode):
- Entry "A" (id 1) and entry "B" (id 2), both baseUrl E.
- Edit "A": editor with initial = A. Rename to "B", Save.
- `_save` clash check: `clash = byName("B")` → entry B (id 2). `clash.id != widget.initial?.id` → 2 != 1 → true. `clash.baseUrl != baseUrl` → E != E → false. → condition false → NOT rejected. Pop result(name "B", baseUrl E).
- The edit caller (Providers section) presumably does `registry.update(CustomProvider(id: 1, name: "B", ...))` → now TWO entries named "B" on endpoint E → the ambiguity this PR is meant to eliminate, plus `byName("B")` returns the first → future reconnects would update the wrong entry.

So the "same endpoint = re-connect shape" rule conflates CONNECT (add flow, where updating by name is right) and EDIT (where renaming to a colliding name on the same endpoint should be rejected). Unless the edit caller rejects it... Let me check the ProvidersSection edit handler.

Very valuable context. Key facts about CLI parity:

1. CLI `find(name)` is case-insensitive — the new app `byName` case-insensitivity matches the CLI. ✓ parity claim holds.

2. CLI's `add` **throws on reserved (catalog) names** — "the interactive name prompts reject these names already, this is the last line of defense". The app's new `landProviderResult` and fa_ui `ProviderRegistry.add` have NO reserved-name guard, and the app prompts don't reject catalog names (`openai`, `codemie`, `kimi`...). BUT does the app registry persist to the same `providers.json` / config as the CLI? The fa_ui ProviderRegistry persists to `providers.json` under ExecutionEnv.cwd — a DIFFERENT store than the CLI's config.yaml customProviders. So catalog-name shadowing (`/provider <name>` routing) is CLI-only and doesn't cross stores. So missing catalog-name rejection in the app is NOT a parity bug per se (the CLI rationale is `/provider` routing, which doesn't exist in the app). OK — not an issue beyond CLI-vs-app store separation.

3. However `isUsableCustomProviderName` — the CLI validates names against `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+:@-]*$` because names with `?`/whitespace/quotes corrupt YAML (issue #555). But the app registry persists to providers.json (JSON), not YAML. Wait — actually is the app's ProviderRegistry writing config.yaml or providers.json? `static const fileName = 'providers.json'`. So YAML corruption is not a concern for the app store. But wait — do app-created providers end up in the CLI's config? The PR description mentions "same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (FA_KEY_<HOST> hydration)" — implying keychain slots ARE shared with the CLI, but the provider entries themselves live in providers.json (app) vs config.yaml customProviders (CLI). Two different stores. OK.

So the missing name-validation in the app prompt is a low-severity observation: a name with leading/trailing whitespace is trimmed; but names like `?`, `my provider` (space), `#work`, emoji are allowed by the app while the CLI would reject them. Key facts:

1. `ProviderRegistry.add` does NOT replace on name clash — it always appends. So the CLI "add-replaces-on-name-clash" convention is implemented only inside `landProviderResult`, NOT in `registry.add` itself. All OTHER app callers of `registry.add` remain unconditional adds: they can still mint same-name duplicates (no guard), and once duplicates exist, `byName` silently targets the first. Confirmed inconsistency.

2. `rememberKey` — interesting: with keychain, `rememberKey(id, key)` stores the key under `keyNameFor(baseUrl)` — HOST-scoped. This is the documented known follow-up: two same-host entries share one keychain slot. Also notice: `rememberKey` from `landProviderResult`/`saveCodemieConnection` → keychain write keyed by baseUrl host. The second CodeMie account's cookie would OVERWRITE the first account's keychain slot. And `add()` re-picks up `remembered` key from the shared slot. This is acknowledged in the PR description as a known follow-up — OK, documented. But worth surfacing in review as a data-loss-ish caveat: account A's persisted key is silently replaced by account B's after restart. Documented = not blocking, but I might list under "known limitations acknowledged by the author" in the general comment.

With multi-account coexistence, TWO entries may serve the same preset endpoint (e.g., two OpenRouter accounts added as "OpenRouter Work" / "OpenRouter Personal" via the picker — allowed now!). Then `_editPreset` (tapping the preset row in the Providers section, not a custom row) updates the FIRST by URL and renames it to whatever name is typed — could silently rename the wrong account AND collide names. Pre-existing logic, but the PR's new multi-account world makes its ambiguity worse. Worth an IMPORTANT/SUGGESTION. Actually the picker prefill fix means re-adding via preset tile targets the FIRST entry's name too (`byBaseUrl` first match). Editing the SECOND account is only possible through its custom row (`_editCustom`) — which works (initial set, by-id update). OK.

- Entries: "Work" (id 1, endpoint E), "Personal" (id 2, endpoint E) — both created via the new multi-account flow.
- User edits "Personal" and renames it to "work" → clash check: byName("work") → entry 1; clash.id(1) != initial.id(2) → true; clash.baseUrl(E) != baseUrl(E) → FALSE → no rejection → update lands: entry 2 renamed "work" → registry now has TWO entries named "Work"/"work" on E → every picker shows two indistinguishable rows (the ambiguity the PR set out to kill), and `byName("work")` now returns the first → a later CodeMie/re-connect landing targets the wrong entry.

This is a genuine correctness gap in the invariant enforcement: the editor cannot distinguish "add/connect" from "edit" contexts, and the same-endpoint allowance is correct only for add/connect. That's the clean fix: `if (clash != null && clash.id != widget.initial?.id && (widget.initial == null ? clash.baseUrl != baseUrl : true))`. Right — in edit mode, renaming to any other entry's name should be rejected. That's the actionable suggestion.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
