- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

  (en/ru defaults resolved from the locale, host-overridable via
  `FaUiStringsScope`) — never the app's gen-l10n. App-level concerns are
  injected: the active connection is the `FaChatConnection` interface,
  on-device engine routes are `FaOnDeviceRoute` builders, the apply
  callback carries `FaChatModelConfig`, and named-key resolution goes
  through the `FaUiHost.keyResolver` hook. `flutter_app` consumes it via
  path dep + thin `export` shims at the old paths; the app's
  `lib/ui/screens/providers_section.dart` additionally keeps a
  `DefaultChatModelSection` ADAPTER (old constructor) wiring `AgentService`,
  `LastConnectionStore`, and the on-device engines into the package flow.
- `flutter_app/` — Flutter chat example. Layout: `lib/main.dart`
  (entrypoint + BootstrapScreen: auto-connects the restored last connection
  when its key resolves, else SetupScreen), `lib/ui/` (`app_theme.dart` —
  shim re-exporting the fa_ui theme; `markdown_style.dart`, `screens/`,
  `widgets/`),
  `lib/services/` (agent service, stores, upload, secrets, project mount,
  vision, `theme_controller.dart` theme-mode persistence + `FahThemeScope`;
  `session_keys_store.dart`/`keychain_store.dart`/`provider_registry.dart`/
  `media_models_store.dart`/`vision_models.dart` are shim re-exports of the
  fa_ui stores), `lib/sandbox/` (env,
  shells, wasm, git, fs persistence), feature dirs
  `lib/apps|gemma|webllm|transformers_js|l10n/`. All lib-internal imports
  are absolute `package:fa/...` — no relative imports.
- `flutter_app/lib/ui/markdown_style.dart` (shim re-export of
  `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/markdown_style.dart`) — beyond
  package screen takes as hooks — the settings route (`settingsBuilder` →
  `SettingsScreen`), the files panel (`fileBrowserBuilder` → `FileBrowser`
  with env/fsRevision), the `open_app` launcher (`service.appLauncher` →
  `FaChatHost.appLauncher` when set, else `pushJsApp`), and the composer
  test fakes (`composerBuilder` → the app's `ChatComposer` adapter).
  Composer changes must keep the chat goldens pixel-identical.
- `flutter_app/lib/l10n/` — gen-l10n: `app_en.arb` + `app_ru.arb` →
  `AppLocalizations` (generated, never edit; `flutter gen-l10n`). UI copy
  via `context.l10n.<key>` (`l10n_ext.dart`); locale follows system.
  `test/l10n_guard_test.dart` hard-fails on hardcoded widget strings, en/ru
  key drift, placeholder mismatches, missing keys — opt out per line with

  strings stay literal).
- `flutter_app/test/golden/` — golden tests (see MANDATORY section below).

(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

Fine. And when apiKey non-empty → `||` makes it true, then rememberKey sets it true. So the `||` is redundant-but-harmless. Not worth flagging.

# Changelog

## 1.0.472

- feat(818): herdr integration — fa as a supported herdr agent. The
  canonical detection manifest (`docs/integrations/herdr/fa.toml`) keys
  herdr's `working/blocked/idle` classification on the S3 band-composer
  chrome and the four prompt-zone sheets; `not` gates keep the
  never-unmounting composer gutter from reading idle under the busy row.
  Fixture transcripts captured from the real renderers live under
  `docs/integrations/herdr/fixtures/`, and
  `herdr_detection_test.dart` transliterates herdr's matcher (regions,
  gates, priority arbitration) to keep the manifest and fixtures honest.
  The herdr agent skill (`docs/integrations/herdr/SKILL.md`, installed
  by herdr into `~/.fah/skills/herdr/`) is first-party, `HERDR_ENV`-
  guarded and inert outside herdr; `herdr_skill_test.dart` proves
  discovery, rendering, env passthrough, resume by session id and name,
  and zero regression without herdr. herdr's pane restore re-attaches
  killed panes with the existing `fa --session <id|name>` contract — no
  new fa surface needed. Side fix: `process_probe_io.dart` now honors
  its documented never-throws contract — the old code let a
  `ProcessException` from the `ps` spawn itself (hardened runtimes,
  sandboxes) crash the waiting manifest reconcile; the probes now
  degrade to the documented null ("unverifiable") path.

- fix(env): `LocalExecutionEnv` forwards `renamePath` — kernel-mode cube
  exec was dead since #803's atomic profile restage (the
  `RenamableFileSystem` capability probe failed at the base env), making
  every kernel-backend bash call fail with "profile staging failed" and
  keeping the macOS nested-rw integration gate red on darwin dev

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

the flag) — `golden_test_setup.dart` loads the real `Inter` and
  `JetBrainsMono` families from `test/assets/fonts/` (test-only copies
  of flutter_app's bundled TTFs; the package itself ships no font
  assets) plus the bundled MaterialIcons font, so goldens render real
  glyphs; review every changed PNG after regenerating.
  Package strings live in `FaUiStrings`
  (en/ru defaults resolved from the locale, host-overridable via
  `FaUiStringsScope`) — never the app's gen-l10n. App-level concerns are
  injected: the active connection is the `FaChatConnection` interface,
  on-device engine routes are `FaOnDeviceRoute` builders, the apply
  callback carries `FaChatModelConfig`, and named-key resolution goes
  through the `FaUiHost.keyResolver` hook. `flutter_app` consumes it via
  path dep + thin `export` shims at the old paths; the app's
  `lib/ui/screens/providers_section.dart` additionally keeps a
  `DefaultChatModelSection` ADAPTER (old constructor) wiring `AgentService`,
  `LastConnectionStore`, and the on-device engines into the package flow.
- `flutter_app/` — Flutter chat example. Layout: `lib/main.dart`
  (entrypoint + BootstrapScreen: auto-connects the restored last connection
  when its key resolves, else SetupScreen), `lib/ui/` (`app_theme.dart` —
  shim re-exporting the fa_ui theme; `markdown_style.dart`, `screens/`,
  `widgets/`),
  `lib/services/` (agent service, stores, upload, secrets, project mount,
  vision, `theme_controller.dart` theme-mode persistence + `FahThemeScope`;
  `session_keys_store.dart`/`keychain_store.dart`/`provider_registry.dart`/
  `media_models_store.dart`/`vision_models.dart` are shim re-exports of the
  fa_ui stores), `lib/sandbox/` (env,
  shells, wasm, git, fs persistence), feature dirs
  `lib/apps|gemma|webllm|transformers_js|l10n/`. All lib-internal imports
  are absolute `package:fa/...` — no relative imports.
- `flutter_app/lib/ui/markdown_style.dart` (shim re-export of
  `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/markdown_style.dart`) — beyond
  package screen takes as hooks — the settings route (`settingsBuilder` →
  `SettingsScreen`), the files panel (`fileBrowserBuilder` → `FileBrowser`
  with env/fsRevision), the `open_app` launcher (`service.appLauncher` →
  `FaChatHost.appLauncher` when set, else `pushJsApp`), and the composer
  test fakes (`composerBuilder` → the app's `ChatComposer` adapter).
  Composer changes must keep the chat goldens pixel-identical.
- `flutter_app/lib/l10n/` — gen-l10n: `app_en.arb` + `app_ru.arb` →

  strings stay literal).
- `flutter_app/test/golden/` — golden tests (see MANDATORY section below).

All green. Now let me do a final check on a couple of remaining review threads:

1. **`showCodeMieNamePrompt` — second-account key overwrite in the Keychain** — documented known follow-up ✓ (mentioned in PR description).

2. **Test coverage gaps**: Are there tests pinning the EDIT-path rename collision? No — the new tests cover (a) coexistence, (b) cross-endpoint clash in editor, (c) same-name+endpoint reconnect update, (d) renamed entry prefill. The same-endpoint rename collision in EDIT mode is unpinned (and broken, per my analysis). Also no test for `saveCodemieConnection` update branch ignoring the `name` param.

3. **`landProviderResult` requiresKey quirk**: `requiresKey: existing.requiresKey || result.apiKey.isNotEmpty` — on the update landing, this can only flip false→true. `rememberKey` later flips the marker based on key presence anyway (rememberKey sets requiresKey = key.isNotEmpty). Actually `rememberKey(id, '')` REMOVES the session key and flips requiresKey to false. In `landProviderResult`, `result.apiKey.isEmpty` → rememberKey not called → requiresKey stays as existing's. Fine. And when apiKey non-empty → `||` makes it true, then rememberKey sets it true. So the `||` is redundant-but-harmless. Not worth flagging.

4. **The empty-string model semantics asymmetry**: On the ADD path in `landProviderResult`, empty modelId stays empty (documented as optional). On update, empty = "keep". OK, documented.

5. **`showCodeMieNamePrompt` — no reserved/usable-name validation** (CLI parity gap): The CLI's `_askConnectProviderName` validates `isUsableCustomProviderName` and rejects catalog names. The app dialog and the fa_ui editor don't. The app registry (providers.json) is separate from the CLI config.yaml customProviders, so no cross-store corruption. But names like `?` or names with spaces CAN now be created in the app — the CLI's concern (issue #555 yaml corruption) doesn't apply to providers.json. Low severity — SUGGESTION noting parity is partial (name validation missing; harmless today because stores are separate).

Actually wait — one more check on `byName` asymmetry: `name.trim().toLowerCase()` vs `provider.name.toLowerCase()` (no trim on stored). The editor trims before saving, CodeMie prompt trims. But the CLI entries or hand-edited providers.json could hold untrimmed names. Cosmetic. I'll fold it into the same SUGGESTION or skip. I'll skip — too minor, and could be seen as noise. Actually I'll mention briefly in the same comment as a nit? No — keep comments focused.

6. **The `_completeSignIn` — model/cookie for existingByName targeting a DIFFERENT entry than the by-URL `existing`**: Scenario — entries "A" (E) and "B" (E). SSO re-login lands existing (by URL) = "A" → prefill "A" → model preselected = A's model. User types "B" → target = B (E) → update B with the NEW cookie + the model picked (which was preselected from A!). B's model gets silently replaced by A's model unless the user manually re-picks. Edge case; user actively typed a different name, mild UX surprise. Not worth blocking; maybe skip — the model picker on a re-login shows preselected A's model and the user can change it. I'll skip this one (too speculative).

7. **The PR description mentions `pushProviderEditor` used by "the Providers section, the default-chat-model picker, and the media slot editor"** — all now land via `landProviderResult` ✓ (verified in code).

8. **Security check**: 
   - No secrets logged: `saveCodemieConnection` — the existing secret-redaction in AgentConfig; tests pin no-log ✓.
   - No new dependencies ✓.
   - No workflow changes ✓.
   - Error text interpolates `clash.baseUrl` (user's own data) into UI — fine.
   - The dialog error message shows the clashing endpoint URL — information the user already owns. Fine.

9. **Performance**: byName/byBaseUrl are O(n) linear scans over a handful of providers — fine.

10. **Backward compatibility**: `saveCodemieConnection` gained a REQUIRED `name` param — breaking for external callers. Check: it's in flutter_app/lib/services — app-internal API. All callers updated (grep showed only the two call sites + tests) ✓. `ProviderEditorPage` gained optional params — non-breaking ✓. `landProviderResult` new public API in fa_ui — exported? Check fa_ui.dart exports provider_editor_page.dart: `pushProviderEditor` is used as `faui.pushProviderEditor` — so the barrel exports it; `landProviderResult` becomes public API of the package automatically. Should it be documented/changelog'd? CHANGELOG.md — did the PR update it? The diff has NO changelog entry. Let me check AGENTS.md whether CHANGELOG updates are required per feature. Let me grep.

11. **Diff hygiene**: big dart-format churn in `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart` (re-indenting 2 tests + 1 group — ~160 lines) obscures the real changes (3 name params + 2 new tests + Continue taps). Mixed concerns in one commit. SUGGESTION.

# Changelog

## 1.0.472

- feat(818): herdr integration — fa as a supported herdr agent. The
  canonical detection manifest (`docs/integrations/herdr/fa.toml`) keys
  herdr's `working/blocked/idle` classification on the S3 band-composer
  chrome and the four prompt-zone sheets; `not` gates keep the
  never-unmounting composer gutter from reading idle under the busy row.
  Fixture transcripts captured from the real renderers live under
  `docs/integrations/herdr/fixtures/`, and
  `herdr_detection_test.dart` transliterates herdr's matcher (regions,
  gates, priority arbitration) to keep the manifest and fixtures honest.
  The herdr agent skill (`docs/integrations/herdr/SKILL.md`, installed
  by herdr into `~/.fah/skills/herdr/`) is first-party, `HERDR_ENV`-
  guarded and inert outside herdr; `herdr_skill_test.dart` proves
  discovery, rendering, env passthrough, resume by session id and name,
  and zero regression without herdr. herdr's pane restore re-attaches
  killed panes with the existing `fa --session <id|name>` contract — no
  new fa surface needed. Side fix: `process_probe_io.dart` now honors
  its documented never-throws contract — the old code let a
  `ProcessException` from the `ps` spawn itself (hardened runtimes,
  sandboxes) crash the waiting manifest reconcile; the probes now
  degrade to the documented null ("unverifiable") path.

- fix(env): `LocalExecutionEnv` forwards `renamePath` — kernel-mode cube
  exec was dead since #803's atomic profile restage (the
  `RenamableFileSystem` capability probe failed at the base env), making
  every kernel-backend bash call fail with "profile staging failed" and
  keeping the macOS nested-rw integration gate red on darwin dev

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

This is acknowledged in the PR description as a known follow-up — OK, documented. BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. ## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

With multi-account coexistence, TWO entries may serve the same preset endpoint (e.g., two OpenRouter accounts added as "OpenRouter Work" / "OpenRouter Personal" via the picker — allowed now!). Then `_editPreset` (tapping the preset row in the Providers section, not a custom row) updates the FIRST by URL and renames it to whatever name is typed — could silently rename the wrong account AND collide names. Pre-existing logic, but the PR's new multi-account world makes its ambiguity worse. Worth an IMPORTANT/SUGGESTION. - Entries: "Work" (id 1, endpoint E), "Personal" (id 2, endpoint E) — both created via the new multi-account flow.

The fix: reject a name clash on the same endpoint when `clash.id != widget.initial?.id` too (i.e., a different entry on the same endpoint owns the name). That's the clean fix: `if (clash != null && clash.id != widget.initial?.id && (widget.initial == null ? clash.baseUrl != baseUrl : true))`. Right — in edit mode, renaming to any other entry's name should be rejected. That's the actionable suggestion.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

💡 **SUGGESTION: TextEditingController created inside the dialog builder — never disposed, recreated on route rebuild**

Two lifecycle issues with creating the controller inside `showDialog`'s `builder`:

1. **No `dispose()`** — every dialog open leaks a controller. The sibling step in this very flow (`CodeMieModelPickerPage` in `codemie_sso_pickers.dart`) uses a proper `StatefulWidget` with `initState`/`dispose`, as does `ProviderEditorPage`; the closest precedent (`app_launcher_screen._renameFolder`) shares the same flaw and shouldn't be copied.
2. **Builder re-runs** — if the dialog route itself rebuilds (route-level `setState`, e.g. during the open/close animation tick or a `MediaQuery`-driven route rebuild), the builder closure runs again and mints a **fresh controller**, silently resetting the field to `initial` mid-typing. The `StatefulBuilder` only scopes `setState` for the error text, not the controller creation.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `name` is dead in the update branch of `saveCodemieConnection`**

`name` is now a **required** parameter, but the update branch ignores it and keeps `existing.name`:

```dart
if (existing != null) {
  final updated = CustomProvider(
    id: existing.id,
    name: existing.name, // ← `name` unused here
    ...
```

It only works because `_completeSignIn` pre-resolves `existing` **by name** (`existingByName`) before calling. That implicit two-step contract is easy to break: a future caller passing `existing` (e.g. resolved by URL, like `_completeExtensionSignin` still does) plus a user-typed `name` will silently drop the typed name with no error. Either use `name` in the update branch (keeping the entry's identity is fine — but then say why), or downgrade `name` to optional with a doc comment stating it is only honored on the add path, and assert/log the mismatch.

💡 **SUGGESTION: extension branch updates the FIRST by-URL match — ambiguous once multi-account entries exist**

This change correctly keeps the extension (cookie-jar) branch name-step-free — one browser jar carries one session. But the update target here comes from `_completeExtensionSignin`'s lookup:

```dart
final existing = registry.providers
    .where((p) => p.baseUrl == baseUrl)
    .firstOrNull;
```

After this PR, several entries can legitimately share one CodeMie endpoint (second accounts minted via the SSO name step). An extension re-login will then overwrite the **first** entry in insertion order — an arbitrary account — updating its `modelId` and keeping its name, while the SSO branch now lands deterministically by name (`registry.byName`). Consider resolving the target the same way (e.g. by the name of the entry whose key/session was last used, or at least documenting that extension re-logins pick the first entry by URL), so the two CodeMie surfaces don't diverge in which account they refresh.

💡 **SUGGESTION: ~160 lines of pure `dart format` churn mixed into the feature diff**

Hunks like this one re-indent the two `issue #623` tests and the whole `issue #586` group without any semantic change (~160 of the 163 deletions). The real changes in this file — the three new `name:` arguments, the two new `#977` widget tests, and the `Continue` taps — become hard to spot for reviewers and will pollute `git blame`/`git log -L` for these tests.

The reformat is legitimate output of `dart format` (which the repo mandates), but it is unrelated to #977. For future PRs, consider landing mechanical reformat as a separate preceding commit (`style: dart format …`) so the feature diff stays reviewable. No action required on this PR if a split is impractical now.

- **State**: open

- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment_codemie_name_prompt_controller.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: TextEditingController created inside the dialog builder — never disposed, recreated on route rebuild**

Two lifecycle issues with creating the controller inside `showDialog`'s `builder`:

1. **No `dispose()`** — every dialog open leaks a controller. The sibling step in this very flow (`CodeMieModelPickerPage` in `codemie_sso_pickers.dart`) uses a proper `StatefulWidget` with `initState`/`dispose`, as does `ProviderEditorPage`; the closest precedent (`app_launcher_screen._renameFolder`) shares the same flaw and shouldn't be copied.
2. **Builder re-runs** — if the dialog route itself rebuilds (route-level `setState`, e.g. during the open/close animation tick or a `MediaQuery`-driven route rebuild), the builder closure runs again and mints a **fresh controller**, silently resetting the field to `initial` mid-typing. The `StatefulBuilder` only scopes `setState` for the error text, not the controller creation.

Suggested fix: extract a small private `StatefulWidget` (like `CodeMieModelPickerPage`) that owns the controller and its `dispose`, or at minimum create the controller before `showDialog` and add `.whenComplete(controller.dispose)` on the awaited future.
"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `name` is dead in the update branch of `saveCodemieConnection`**

`name` is now a **required** parameter, but the update branch ignores it and keeps `existing.name`:

```dart
if (existing != null) {
  final updated = CustomProvider(
    id: existing.id,
    name: existing.name, // ← `name` unused here
    ...
```

It only works because `_completeSignIn` pre-resolves `existing` **by name** (`existingByName`) before calling. That implicit two-step contract is easy to break: a future caller passing `existing` (e.g. resolved by URL, like `_completeExtensionSignin` still does) plus a user-typed `name` will silently drop the typed name with no error. Either use `name` in the update branch (keeping the entry's identity is fine — but then say why), or downgrade `name` to optional with a doc comment stating it is only honored on the add path, and assert/log the mismatch.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: extension branch updates the FIRST by-URL match — ambiguous once multi-account entries exist**

This change correctly keeps the extension (cookie-jar) branch name-step-free — one browser jar carries one session. But the update target here comes from `_completeExtensionSignin`'s lookup:

```dart
final existing = registry.providers
    .where((p) => p.baseUrl == baseUrl)
    .firstOrNull;
```

After this PR, several entries can legitimately share one CodeMie endpoint (second accounts minted via the SSO name step). An extension re-login will then overwrite the **first** entry in insertion order — an arbitrary account — updating its `modelId` and keeping its name, while the SSO branch now lands deterministically by name (`registry.byName`). Consider resolving the target the same way (e.g. by the name of the entry whose key/session was last used, or at least documenting that extension re-logins pick the first entry by URL), so the two CodeMie surfaces don't diverge in which account they refresh.

## Automated Code Review — APPROVE (2 should-fix, 4 suggestions)

**Summary**: The #977 fix is solid where it lands — the CodeMie SSO name step, the shared `landProviderResult` add/update landing, `byName`/`byBaseUrl` registry lookups, and the en+ru clash string all check out, and I verified the claims locally: fa_ui multi-account/registry/picker/section/strings suites pass, app `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart` 34/34 pass, `dart analyze` clean on all changed files, and the CLI-parity conventions (`_askConnectProviderName` retry-on-cross-endpoint-clash, case-insensitive `find`, `_entryForBaseUrl`) are faithfully mirrored.

**Key Issues** (details in inline comments):
1. 🟡 IMPORTANT — `ProviderEditorPage._save` allows renaming an entry onto a sibling's name **on the same endpoint** in edit mode → two same-name entries (the exact ambiguity this PR removes); `byName` then mis-targets from then on (`comment_provider_editor_rename_clash.md`).
2. 🟡 IMPORTANT — the landing fix is not applied to all app add-provider entry points (unchanged code): `onboarding_screen._persistKeyBased` and `settings.dart _addProvider`/`_addProviderFromCta` still land with unconditional `registry.add` (`_addProvider*` don't even pass `registry` to the editor, so the new clash check never runs) — a re-add there still duplicates. Same class: `ProvidersSection._editPreset` keeps its own by-URL landing.
3. 💡 SUGGESTION — name-prompt controller lifecycle; `name` param dead in `saveCodemieConnection`'s update branch; extension branch's arbitrary first-by-URL target; ~160 lines of pure `dart format` churn in the test file.

**Also noted** (acknowledged by the author, fine to defer): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot (`FA_KEY_<HOST>`), so a second CodeMie account's cookie overwrites the first account's persisted key after restart.

**Next Steps**:
1. Tighten the editor clash rule for edit mode (reject any name owned by another entry when `initial != null`) + add a widget test.
2. Route the onboarding key-based landing and the two settings-screen add paths through `landProviderResult` (and pass `registry` to their editors) — or explicitly scope them out of #977.
3. Optional: dispose/own the name-prompt controller, use or drop `name` in the update branch, align the extension-branch target resolution, split the reformat churn.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 984
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/984
- **Title**: feat(#977): provider name step + multi-account coexistence in app add-provider flow
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-977` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +650
- **Deletions**: -163
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:30:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:41:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #977

## What collapsed (verified)

Two entry points mapped every same-type provider onto ONE entry:

- **CodeMie SSO flow** (`runCodemieSsoFlow` → `saveCodemieConnection`): the org URL is fixed to the default, so every login produced the same `baseUrl`; the save looked the existing entry up **by URL** and updated it in place. A second login — even a second account — overwrote the one CodeMie entry (name, model, key). No name step existed (CLI `/provider codemie` asks one).
- **Generic editor path** (`AddProviderPresetPickerPage` → `ProviderEditorPage` → `registry.add`): always **added** — a re-add of an existing endpoint duplicated it, and a display name already used by an entry on another endpoint was silently accepted (two indistinguishable rows in every picker).

AIIN already names entries after the account email with de-dup + name-scoped key slots (`_finishAiinConnect`) — its desktop connect coexists correctly and needed no change.

## Change (CLI parity: `_askConnectProviderName` / `_entryForBaseUrl`)

- `ProviderRegistry.byName` / `byBaseUrl` — the CLI `find` / `_entryForBaseUrl` conventions as shared lookups.
- Editor save rejects a name used by an entry on a **different** endpoint (inline error, en+ru strings); same name + same endpoint = the re-connect shape.
- `landProviderResult` — shared add/update landing used by `pushProviderEditor` and the preset picker: a name+endpoint match updates in place (id, dropdown selections and an empty model field survive; key refreshed), anything else adds a fresh entry (second account on a shared endpoint).
- Preset picker prefills the editor name from the existing entry on the preset endpoint — a **renamed** entry reconnects without duplication.
- CodeMie SSO name step (`showCodeMieNamePrompt`, after credentials/model pick): prefilled with the existing entry name (re-login) or the org host; cross-endpoint clash rejected inline; cancel falls back to the prefill (the CLI's credentials-already-minted convention for OAuth/SSO). Fresh name on the same org = second account entry. Extension (cookie-jar) branch keeps the host name — one browser jar carries one session.

## Evidence

- New fa_ui `provider_multi_account_test.dart` pins: (a) two same-type entries with different names coexist in the Providers section, (b) cross-endpoint name clash rejected inline with nothing saved, (c) reconnect-by-URL updates instead of duplicating (same id, model preserved, key refreshed), plus renamed-entry re-add via the preset prefill. `flutter test` fa_ui scoped suites (multi-account, registry, picker, section, editor-models, strings): **63+38 pass, 0 fail**.
- App `codemie_sso_flow_steps_test.dart`: **34 pass** — incl. new end-to-end "second account on the same org becomes its OWN entry" and "name used by another ENDPOINT is rejected inline".
- `dart analyze` clean on all changed files (remaining infos are the test file's pre-existing `(_, __)` style).

Known follow-up (out of scope here): same-host entries share the host-scoped Keychain slot after restart (`FA_KEY_<HOST>` hydration); AIIN already persists name-scoped slots, CodeMie second accounts currently resolve the latest host-scoped key after a restart until re-auth.

No CI dispatched or rerun.

This is a genuine correctness gap in the invariant enforcement: the editor cannot distinguish "add/connect" from "edit" contexts, and the same-endpoint allowance is correct only for add/connect. The fix: reject a name clash on the same endpoint when `clash.id != widget.initial?.id` too (i.e., a different entry on the same endpoint owns the name). So the stricter rule needs a mode flag (create vs edit) — e.g., only allow same-endpoint name takeover when `initial == null` (create/re-connect) — in EDIT mode (initial != null), reject ANY name owned by another entry (regardless of endpoint). That's the clean fix: `if (clash != null && clash.id != widget.initial?.id && (widget.initial == null ? clash.baseUrl != baseUrl : true))`. Right — in edit mode, renaming to any other entry's name should be rejected. That's the actionable suggestion.

  `herdr_detection_test.dart` transliterates herdr's matcher (regions,
  gates, priority arbitration) to keep the manifest and fixtures honest.
  The herdr agent skill (`docs/integrations/herdr/SKILL.md`, installed
  by herdr into `~/.fah/skills/herdr/`) is first-party, `HERDR_ENV`-
  guarded and inert outside herdr; `herdr_skill_test.dart` proves
  discovery, rendering, env passthrough, resume by session id and name,
  and zero regression without herdr. herdr's pane restore re-attaches
  killed panes with the existing `fa --session <id|name>` contract — no
  new fa surface needed. Side fix: `process_probe_io.dart` now honors
  its documented never-throws contract — the old code let a
  `ProcessException` from the `ps` spawn itself (hardened runtimes,
  sandboxes) crash the waiting manifest reconcile; the probes now
  degrade to the documented null ("unverifiable") path.

- fix(env): `LocalExecutionEnv` forwards `renamePath` — kernel-mode cube
  exec was dead since #803's atomic profile restage (the
  `RenamableFileSystem` capability probe failed at the base env), making
  every kernel-backend bash call fail with "profile staging failed" and
  keeping the macOS nested-rw integration gate red on darwin dev

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment_codemie_name_prompt_controller.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: TextEditingController created inside the dialog builder — never disposed, recreated on route rebuild**

Two lifecycle issues with creating the controller inside `showDialog`'s `builder`:

1. **No `dispose()`** — every dialog open leaks a controller. The sibling step in this very flow (`CodeMieModelPickerPage` in `codemie_sso_pickers.dart`) uses a proper `StatefulWidget` with `initState`/`dispose`, as does `ProviderEditorPage`; the closest precedent (`app_launcher_screen._renameFolder`) shares the same flaw and shouldn't be copied.
2. **Builder re-runs** — if the dialog route itself rebuilds (route-level `setState`, e.g. during the open/close animation tick or a `MediaQuery`-driven route rebuild), the builder closure runs again and mints a **fresh controller**, silently resetting the field to `initial` mid-typing. The `StatefulBuilder` only scopes `setState` for the error text, not the controller creation.

Suggested fix: extract a small private `StatefulWidget` (like `CodeMieModelPickerPage`) that owns the controller and its `dispose`, or at minimum create the controller before `showDialog` and add `.whenComplete(controller.dispose)` on the awaited future.
